newsitem.title: USA: RJR Nabisco prevails over Icahn -- analysts.
newsitem.headline: RJR Nabisco prevails over Icahn -- analysts.

text.p: RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp has prevailed over shareholder Carl Icahn, who last night sold his entire 7.3 percent stake in RJR after unsuccessfully agitating for more than a year for the company to split along tobacco and food lines.

Icahn sold his 19.9 million RJR shares at $36.75 each in an off-market deal handled by Goldman Sachs, a trade that reaped Icahn at least $100 million in profit and in effect nullified his proxy fight to replace the RJR board at the annual meeting in April, according to analysts.

"He is no longer a shareholder, so now he can't even get into the annual meeting. He is all done. He accomplished his objective, which was to make a living, to have a good year," said Emanuel Goldman, tobacco analyst at PainWebber.

Martin Feldman of Smith Barney said, "The most important point is it is good for all tobacco equities because (RJR chairman Steven) Goldstone is involved in negotiations pushing for a compromise with the antitobacco lobby and congressional legislation. These are very delicate talks and if Icahn was successful in taking over the RJR board, he could have toppled the applecart."

As for Bennett LeBow, the chairman of Brooke Group Ltd who lauched a simultaneous, though separate, campaign to force a split of RJR, analysts said his position has been substantially weakened without the like-minded Icahn, though he is less likely to sell his roughly one percent of RJR right now because he bought the shares at a higher price than Icahn.
Attempts to reach LeBow and Icahn for additional comment were not immediately successful, and Goldman Sachs declined to provide addtional detail on the huge trade.
In afternoon New York Stock Exchange trade, RJR shares were off 3/4 at 37, near the intraday year-high hit on Monday.
On Monday, RJR traded as high as 38-7/8, then settled back to close at 37-3/4.

"This leaves LeBow absolutely out in the cold. Brooke Group might even cease to exist in the next 24 months. Liggett (Brooke's tobacco unit) continues to lose market share and profitability continues to decline. The fundamentals there are the worst in the industry," Feldman said.
Roy Burry at Oppenheimer & Co, said Icahn "made money after being underwater for a long time. He probably thought he could not win the proxy battle in April, so why throw good money after bad?"
Nabisco Holdings Corp, the packaged food company Icahn wanted completely separated from the tobacco operations, remains 81 percent owned by RJR.
Nabisco shares began trading separately from RJR in January, 1995 at around $26 per share.
In afternoon NYSE trade, Nabisco stock was off 7/8 at 42-1/2.

"LeBow has his own particular agenda, somewhat different from Icahn's. LeBow is in the cigarette business with a company that has had results that have not set the world on fire. He would like to have someone buy his company," Goldman said.
"Icahn championed shareholder value, but for a single shareholder. He made an investment and he is getting a terrific return," he added.

Among other tobacco stocks, Brooke was unchanged at 4-7/8 in very light volume, Philip Morris Cos Inc rose 2-1/8 to 135-5/8, UST Inc added 3/8 to 30-1/8 and B.A.T Industries Plc's U.S.-traded shares were off 7/16 to 17-3/4.
